island.summary: A raw, slightly rugged Aegean island: pale limestone, dry-stone walls, pine and olive on scrub-covered slopes, clear turquoise water and long, rich sunsets. Nature dominates. People live here in a few small, old places built into the land, and nothing is polished for visitors.
island.palette: Pale stone and whitewash, rich pine greens, silvery olive leaves, turquoise shallows and rich blue water further out, warm red earth, and sunset tones of amber, coral, rose and violet.
rules: Mediterranean, never tropical: umbrella pines, olives, cypress, juniper, figs, vines and aromatic herbs. No palms, lagoons or white-sand resort beaches.
Raw rather than manicured: paths are worn, not built; walls are dry stone; paint is faded by salt and sun. Pale rock breaks through the vegetation everywhere.
Nature leads. Buildings and paths are small, old and fitted to the terrain.
Never artificial, fantastical or luxury-resort-like. No roads, vehicles, crowds, signs, hotels, nightlife, industry or dense building.
Human life is slow, social and purposeful: people work, talk and eat together without hurry.
One consistent geography, climate, light and soundscape, believable enough that a listener can imagine standing there.
Every place should make it easier to be completely present.

regions.name: The Cove
regions.summary: The emotional heart of the island: a gently sheltered bay held by rocky headlands and scrub-covered mountain slopes, with pale sand, clear turquoise water and the open sea behind. It belongs to the sunset.

regions.name: The Pine Path
regions.summary: The old walking path from the cove, climbing gently through pines, olives and wild herbs, then curving down past terraces and stone walls towards the village. Worn by generations of feet, never built for visitors.

regions.name: The Fishing Village
regions.summary: An old, modest village of whitewashed and pale stone houses around a small natural harbour, climbing a little into the slopes. Lived-in, unhurried and real: peace through belonging and everyday work.

regions.name: The High Plateau
regions.summary: Broad, open upland in the island's interior, reached by shepherds' tracks beyond the village: thyme, dry grass, scattered pines and pale rock, with the cove, the harbour and the whole sea in view.

places.name: The Cove
places.description: You stand with your feet just inside the water of a gently sheltered bay. The tiniest waves move across your feet and ankles, refreshing but not cold, still holding the warmth of the day, and the wet sand beneath you is firm, smooth and supportive. Ahead, the land rises in uneven green slopes of pine, juniper and scrub, with pale rock breaking through. The rocky, mountainous sides of the cove curve protectively round you and hide the village and the rest of the coast, so the cove feels private but never closed in. To the left, the sun shines brilliantly above the rocky ridge, still high enough that it has not yet begun to set behind it. Behind you is the open sea, calm and glimmering, stretching on as far as you can see.
sights: the sun intensely golden above the rocky ridge to the left
a sky turning amber, coral, red, rose, vivid pink, lavender and violet, with a few thin, wispy clouds catching the colour
the nearest mountains taking on copper, rose and violet tones, with a delicate golden haze softening the distant ridges
exceptionally clear turquoise water over a pale, sandy seabed, with only a few scattered rocks and pebbles
small, colourful fish occasionally moving through the shallows
umbrella pines, olives, cypress, juniper and low shrubs on the slopes, with pale rock breaking through
a narrow gap in the green growth at the far left, where the path begins
sounds: the smallest waves folding onto the shore
faint cicadas further back in the scrub
pine branches moving lightly in the breeze
now and then a fish briefly touching the surface
textures: small waves moving gently across the feet and ankles
water refreshing but not cold, still warm from the day
a very gentle breeze on the face
smells: pine resin drifting down from the slopes
places.timeOfDay: sunset, while the sun is still above the ridge
places.light: Intensely golden sun with a kaleidoscopic sky; the cove itself stays clear and bright, and the open sea behind glimmers softly in the evening light.
places.wayIn: The old path from the village, which comes out as a narrow gap in the vegetation at the far left of the beach.
places.wayOut: That gap in the green at the far left, and the open, pale sand of the beach all around you.
places.feeling: Serenity, presence, liberty and release: nowhere else you would rather be. Not escape through avoidance but freedom through complete presence, part of the landscape: the same breeze that moves the pines touches your face, and the same water that fills the cove moves around your feet. Burdens briefly stop mattering.

places.name: The Cove in the Morning
places.description: The same cove early in the day, before the sun has climbed over the slopes behind the beach. The water is so still it looks like glass, and the sandy floor is clear right out into the bay. You might sit on the cool, pale sand just above the waterline and watch the light reach the far headland first.
sights: glass-still turquoise water
sunlight touching the far headland first
the sandy floor clear beneath the water
the cove still in soft shade
sounds: a near-silent lapping at the waterline
a bird calling once from the pines
textures: the first warmth of the sun on the skin
places.light: Soft, cool shade on the beach, with clear golden light creeping across the headland and the water.
places.wayIn: The path through the gap in the scrub at the far left of the beach.
places.wayOut: The same gap in the green, and the open beach on every side.
places.feeling: Quiet beginning: the island waking slowly, with nothing yet asked of the day.

places.name: The Pine Shade
places.description: At the back of the beach, where the sand meets the slope, an old umbrella pine leans out over the sand and makes a wide circle of shade. Fallen needles soften the sand beneath it. You might sit with your back against the trunk and look out across the bright cove to the open sea.
sights: the broad, flat crown of an umbrella pine
a carpet of pine needles on the sand
the bright cove framed between the trunk and the rocks
pale rock and juniper on the slope behind
sounds: cicadas close by in the scrub
the soft creak of pine branches
places.light: Bright, white Aegean sun on the water, with soft, moving shade beneath the pine.
places.wayIn: A few steps up the beach from the water.
places.wayOut: The open sand in front of you, and the path's gap in the green a short walk to your left.
places.feeling: Rest in the heat of the day; being held by the shade while the whole bright cove stays in view.

places.name: The Warm Rocks
places.description: Where the beach meets the right-hand side of the cove, low, broad slabs of pale rock lie at the level of the sand, worn smooth by the sea. Clear water laps gently at their sides, reaching only to the ankles, with the sandy floor bright beneath it. You might sit on the warmest slab and trail your feet in the shallows.
sights: broad, smooth slabs of pale rock
clear shallows beside them, only up to the ankles
tiny fish in the sunlit water
scrub and juniper growing from cracks in the slope behind
sounds: water lapping softly at the rock
a gull far out over the sea
places.light: Warm, slanting afternoon light; the rock glows pale gold.
places.wayIn: A few steps along the sand from the waterline.
places.wayOut: The flat sand of the beach, right beside the rocks.
places.feeling: Warmth and ease: the sun-heated stone gives the body permission to soften.

places.name: The Path from the Cove
places.description: The path begins as little more than a thinning in the vegetation at the far left of the cove: flat stones, dry earth, pine needles and patches of reddish soil, showing that people have walked this way for generations. It climbs gently inland through umbrella pines, old olives, juniper, rosemary and wild thyme. The ground is uneven but comfortable, and the sound of the sea softens behind you without disappearing. Nothing urges you forward; each bend shows a small detail rather than a spectacle.
sights: flat stones and reddish earth underfoot
pine needles gathered at the sides of the path
sun and shade in patches across the trail
a lizard slipping into a crack in the stone
butterflies resting on flowering herbs
sounds: the sea growing softer through the trees
textures: smooth stones and dry earth underfoot
herbs brushing the legs and releasing their scent
places.light: Warm light filtering through pine branches in moving patches.
places.wayIn: The narrow gap in the green at the far left of the cove.
places.wayOut: Back down the same path to the cove, whose sound you can still hear, or on along the path towards the village.
places.feeling: Transition, discovery and gentle movement; the serenity of the cove carried along, with a growing curiosity that the island holds more than one kind of peace.

places.name: The Cove Glimpse
places.description: A bend in the path, a little way up the hillside, where the pines open and a flat, sun-warmed stone makes a natural seat. Through the gap in the trees behind you, the cove appears small, protected and turquoise, nested into the land, with the open sea spreading beyond it.
sights: the cove small and turquoise between the trunks
pale headlands holding the bay
the open sea, rich blue beyond
a flat stone seat beside the path
sounds: wind in the upper pine branches
the faintest hush of the sea below
a bird moving in the juniper
places.light: Golden, slanting light; the cove glows turquoise in the sun.
places.wayIn: Along the path from the cove, round a gentle bend.
places.wayOut: The path in both directions, wide and plain to see.
places.feeling: Looking back with fondness: seeing how safely the cove sits within the land.

places.name: The Olive Terraces
places.description: As the path comes closer to the village, the first signs of people appear: low dry-stone walls holding small terraces of old, twisted olive trees. An old wooden basket sits beneath one tree. The ground between the trunks is dry grass and red earth, and the terraces step down the slope in wide, gentle bands.
sights: silvery olive leaves turning in the breeze
twisted, ancient trunks
a low dry-stone wall beside the path
an old wooden basket under a tree
sounds: a goat bell far off on the hillside
places.light: Bright sun broken into dapples by olive leaves.
places.wayIn: Along the path from the pines, where the first wall begins.
places.wayOut: The path running between the terraces in both directions.
places.feeling: Simplicity and continuity: land worked gently by many hands over many years.

places.name: The Fig Lane
places.description: The path becomes a narrow lane between weathered stone walls, with fig trees and vines leaning over them. The village is not yet in view, but you can hear and smell it: a faint metallic clink, a rope tapping a mast, a dog barking once, distant conversation and a brief burst of laughter; woodsmoke, bread, grilled fish and something sweet baking. The change from wild land to village happens slowly, step by step.
sights: broad fig leaves over the wall
vines on a simple frame
weathered stone walls on both sides
a glimpse of whitewash ahead
sounds: a rope tapping gently against a mast
textures: warm wall stone under the hand
places.light: Warm, low evening sun along the top of the walls.
places.wayIn: From the Olive Terraces, where the path narrows between walls.
places.wayOut: On into the village, already in earshot, or back up the path to the terraces.
places.feeling: Anticipation and welcome: wilderness gently giving way to company.

places.name: The Harbour
places.description: A small natural harbour with the village built gently round it, in uneven rows of whitewashed and pale stone houses with faded blue, green and sun-softened red shutters. A handful of wooden fishing boats rock on the water, their paint worn by salt and age. Nets dry beside the quay, ropes and baskets sit near the water, and fishermen mend nets while they talk. People are busy, but never rushed.
sights: wooden fishing boats with salt-worn paint
nets drying along the quay
whitewashed houses with faded shutters
coiled ropes and baskets by the water
fishermen mending nets
sounds: water lapping at the harbour wall
places.light: Warm, golden late-day light on whitewash and water.
places.wayIn: Down the Fig Lane into the village and out onto the quay.
places.wayOut: Any of the lanes leading up from the quay, or back the way you came.
places.feeling: Belonging and meaningful work: life here is not rushed through or optimised; people are simply living it.

places.name: The Harbour Taverna
places.description: A small taverna right by the harbour, with simple wooden tables and rush-seated chairs set out under a vine. Friends gather for coffee, food and long conversations; meals are unhurried and work and talk run into each other. You might sit at a table near the water with a small glass and watch the boats.
sights: simple wooden tables under a vine
plates being shared
boats moving gently on the water
a cat stretched out on a warm step
sounds: faint music through an open window
textures: the woven seat of a chair
places.light: Soft, warm light with the sky turning rose over the water.
places.wayIn: A few steps along the quay from the boats.
places.wayOut: The open quay in front, and the lanes behind.
places.feeling: Connection and ease: being among people without needing to do or say anything.

places.name: The Whitewashed Lanes
places.description: Narrow, irregular lanes climb a little from the harbour between whitewashed walls, their stones smoothed by long use. Clay pots of basil and geraniums sit on doorsteps. A neighbour sweeps a step, someone waters herbs outside a door, and a child carries bread home. The lanes are short, and the harbour is always just below.
sights: whitewashed walls and blue doors
clay pots of basil and geraniums
a cat asleep on a warm step
glimpses of harbour at the bottom of each lane
places.light: Bright morning sun on whitewash, with cool shade along one side of each lane.
places.wayIn: Up any lane from the harbour.
places.wayOut: Every lane runs back down to the harbour, in view below.
places.feeling: Simplicity and community: small daily tasks done slowly and well.

places.name: The Bakery Step
places.description: A wide, whitewashed step outside the village bakery, where the wood-fired oven has been lit since before dawn. You might sit on the step with something warm to eat while the village wakes around the harbour below. The bakery door stands open and the lane is right in front of you.
sights: a wide whitewashed step
the open bakery door and the glow of the oven
loaves cooling on a wooden board
boats in the harbour below
sounds: boats knocking gently at the quay
textures: rough, warm plaster at your back
places.light: Soft, clear early sun, and the orange glow of the oven through the door.
places.wayIn: A short walk up the lane from the harbour.
places.wayOut: The lane in front of you, running down to the harbour.
places.feeling: Being cared for in a simple way: warmth, food and the village starting its day.

places.name: The Shepherds' Track
places.description: Beyond the last houses, an old track climbs gently into the hills. The coastal scrub gives way to pines and olive groves, then to wild thyme, dry grasses and exposed pale rock. The track is wide and well worn by goats and shepherds, and the land opens out more with every bend.
sights: a wide, stony track
scattered pines and olives thinning out
wild thyme and dry grasses
pale rock breaking through the hillside
places.light: Clear, open light that turns golden as the afternoon goes on.
places.wayIn: From the top of the village lanes, past the last walls.
places.wayOut: Back down the same track, with the village roofs in sight below.
places.feeling: Spaciousness growing with every step: the coast left behind and the sky opening up.

places.name: The Threshing Floor
places.description: On a broad, level shoulder of the hills sits an old threshing floor: a wide circle of flat stones ringed by a low kerb, unused now and warmed by the sun. Grass grows between the stones. You might sit in the middle, where the whole sky is open above you.
sights: a wide circle of flat, pale stones
grass and thyme between them
rolling hills all around
the sea glinting in the distance
places.light: Long, golden light across the open ground.
places.wayIn: A short side path from the Shepherds' Track.
places.wayOut: The side path back to the track, plain to see across the open ground.
places.feeling: Simplicity and continuity with the past: a quiet place where generations worked, now at rest.

places.name: The High Plateau
places.description: The track ends on a broad natural terrace in the island's interior, wide and level, with an old low stone wall and a simple, weathered shepherd's shelter. You stand well back from where the land begins to slope away. From here you can see the cove far below as a small turquoise shape held by the land, the village and harbour in another direction, and beyond both a vast, calm sea. As twilight comes, the stone still holds the day's warmth while the air turns cooler, and the sky slowly fills with stars, with no artificial light to hide them.
sights: the cove far below, small and turquoise
the village and harbour in another direction, its first lights coming on
a vast, calm sea in the last light
the first stars, then many
a low stone wall and a weathered shepherd's shelter
sounds: a goat bell far off, then quiet
textures: stone still warm from the day
cooler air on the face and arms
smells: a faint trace of salt carried up from the sea
places.timeOfDay: twilight, as the first stars appear
places.light: The last rose and violet light in the west, the village lights below and a sky filling with stars.
places.wayIn: The Shepherds' Track, arriving on the wide, level terrace.
places.wayOut: The same track, easy to follow, with the village lights below to guide you.
places.feeling: Perspective and wonder: the things you worry about are small within something much larger. Awe without feeling insignificant; spaciousness and gentle humility.

places.name: The Thyme Slope
places.description: A broad, gentle slope near the plateau, covered in low, flowering wild thyme and grey sage. Bees work slowly through the flowers, and a few scattered pines give patches of shade. The ground is easy and open, and the track is always in sight.
sights: low cushions of purple-flowering thyme
grey sage
slow bees
a few scattered pines
sounds: a light breeze in the grasses
places.light: Clear, fresh morning light with the whole sky open.
places.wayIn: A step off the Shepherds' Track.
places.wayOut: The track, a few steps away and always in view.
places.feeling: Connection with nature: being one more small, unhurried thing among the bees and flowers.
